title: Employee Onboarding Workflow Template: Free Options
summary: Employee onboarding workflow templates streamline new hire setup. Compare six free options to find the best tool for your team.
body_markdown:
## 3. Activepieces: best for automating onboarding steps across apps


Once you record a hire, Activepieces, whose core is MIT-licensed and which **has 740 integrations** , runs onboarding steps across apps, so you can run a dummy hire through it before a real one arrives.


Each app connects through an integration, and a flow is a trigger followed by steps.


Five flows below cover the handoffs that usually get missed. Each line gives the trigger, the steps and the integration it links to:


- Hire row added in[Google Sheets](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/google-sheets) , the hire record: creates the IT, access and equipment tasks in[Asana](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/asana) , each with an owner and due date.
- Same trigger: posts a welcome message in[Slack](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/slack) , the team chat.
- Same trigger: reminds the manager in Slack before the start date and again if their tasks are still open.
- Same trigger: sends day-one paperwork by[Gmail](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/gmail) . Same trigger: books check-ins in[Google Calendar](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/google-calendar) at 30, 60 and 90 days, so you're prompted at roughly monthly intervals.


You want to see which flow broke, and each one fails separately. That is why there are five.


Before anyone approves a budget, you can build and test all five flows: the[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) Cloud free plan costs $0 with no card, and includes unlimited flows, 1,000 credits a month and up to 5 users.


Because the core is MIT-licensed, you can also self-host it on your own server.


If your HR or badge-access system has no connector, a closed catalogue leaves that step manual until the vendor decides it matters.


Activepieces has 740 integrations, counted from its open source monorepo, and roughly 60% were built by community contributors, so a missing app is often already covered by a integration someone outside the company wrote. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


When a new row lands in the hire sheet, the flow creates one Asana task per setup item, assigns each to its owner, and sets due dates relative to the start date.


The free plan allows unlimited flows and up to 5 users, so you can[start this flow](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Femployee-onboarding-workflow-template-free-options) without paying.


From the same row, one flow posts a welcome in Slack. A second waits until shortly before the start date, then messages the manager with their open tasks. If those tasks are still open, it messages them again.


A Gmail step sends the paperwork and the first-day instructions to the new hire. Calendar steps then create the three check-in events and invite the manager.


### Strengths and limits


You can inspect each run and see where it stopped, because these steps live in the tools your team already uses. That is the strength. The limit is that every flow is something you now maintain.


Check that your apps have an integration before committing. If your HR system already has onboarding built in and your team lives there, use that instead. The same goes if nobody will own the flows after the person who built them leaves.
